The ductility of the HNTTA12 alloy reached 24.5%, which is 256% that of the NHTTA0 alloy.

Furthermore, with decreasing negative mixing enthalpy, the strength of an alloy can increase due to strong enthalpic interactions among the alloying atoms, which is termed negative mixing enthalpy strengthening [16], as shown in Fig. 1 b.

It is clear that, with decreasing enthalpy, the LCO structure is enhanced, exhibiting microstructural transformation from an entropy solid solution to an LCO heterostructure or even to B2 nanoprecipitates, which agrees well with the images in Fig. 1 a.

LCO can promote dislocation cross-slip, enhancing the interaction between dislocations and their accumulation at large tensile strains; sustainable strain hardening can thereby be attained to ensure high ductility of the alloy.
